skill.name: wp-docker
skill.description: Build and manage a local WordPress development stack with Docker Compose, WP-CLI, MariaDB, and setup templates.
skill.summary: Create a Docker-based WordPress development environment with WP-CLI automation.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: Most static hits in SKILL.md are markdown code fences or inline command documentation, but several documented Docker Compose and WP-CLI workflows are real external command execution. The main security concerns are weak default credentials, database password defaults in Docker Compose, destructive volume-removal commands, and the setup script printing the admin password.

remediation.suggestion: Require the caller to provide a strong admin password or generate one securely instead of defaulting to password123.

remediation.issue: Administrator password is printed after setup
remediation.suggestion: Do not echo the admin password to the terminal. Print only the username and login URL, or write secrets to a protected local file only after explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Weak default database credentials in Docker Compose
remediation.suggestion: Remove weak password defaults and require DB_PASSWORD and DB_ROOT_PASSWORD to be set through a local environment file with safe permissions.

remediation.issue: Destructive Docker volume command is documented near routine lifecycle commands
remediation.suggestion: Separate docker-compose down -v into a clearly marked destructive recovery section and require backup guidance before use.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Default WordPress Admin Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The setup script defaults ADMIN_USER to admin and ADMIN_PASSWORD to password123 when arguments are omitted. This can create a predictable administrator account if used beyond a private local environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default administrator username and password are explicit in the script. Predictable admin credentials are a direct account compromise risk if the site is reachable.

semantic_findings.title: Admin Password Printed to Terminal Output
semantic_findings.description: The setup script prints the administrator password at completion. Terminal logs, transcripts, or shared console output could expose the generated site credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly echoes Password: $ADMIN_PASSWORD after setup. This is clear credential disclosure in command output.

content.value_statement: WordPress setup can be slow when every project needs containers, database settings, and plugin setup. This skill provides Docker Compose templates and WP-CLI workflows for repeatable local development.
actual_capabilities: Copies Docker Compose, WP-CLI setup, and PHP upload configuration templates into a project.
Starts a local WordPress stack with MariaDB, WordPress, and WP-CLI services.
Runs WP-CLI commands for installation, plugin setup, themes, pages, options, and database tasks.
Documents common Docker Compose operations for logs, rebuilds, restarts, and health checks.
Supports local migration workflows using database export, import, and URL replacement commands.
limitations: Targets local development and is not a hardened production deployment guide.
Requires Docker Compose, shell access, and permission to run container commands.
Uses example credentials that must be replaced before any shared or public environment.
Does not perform vulnerability scanning of installed WordPress plugins or themes.

use_cases.title: Launch a local WordPress project
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable Docker Compose stack for a new WordPress site with database and WP-CLI access.

use_cases.title: Automate baseline site setup
use_cases.description: Install WordPress, activate common plugins, configure permalinks, and create starter pages through WP-CLI.

use_cases.title: Practice migration tasks locally
use_cases.description: Use documented WP-CLI commands to export, import, and replace URLs in a development database.

prompt_templates.title: Create a new local site
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a fresh project folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-docker skill to set up a local WordPress development environment for my project. Explain each command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Install WordPress with custom details
prompt_templates.scenario: Site setup with chosen URL, title, admin user, and email.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the wp-docker setup workflow for a site named Project Demo at http://localhost:8080. Ask me for secure admin credentials before running setup.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Docker stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the wp-docker Docker Compose and setup script templates for local development risks. Suggest safer values for credentials and exposed ports.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a local migration test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for database migration rehearsal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wp-docker to plan a local WordPress migration test. Include database import, URL replacement, cache flush, and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Set up a local WordPress environment for a new client site.
output: A Docker Compose stack is prepared for WordPress, MariaDB, and WP-CLI.
The assistant asks for secure admin credentials before running the setup script.
The site is available locally after containers start and WordPress installation completes.

output_examples.input: Show me how to migrate a site into this local stack.
output: The assistant outlines export, import, URL replacement, and cache flush steps.
It identifies which commands affect the database before execution.
It recommends taking backups before destructive or irreversible operations.

best_practices: Replace all example passwords and admin values before running the setup script.
Use the stack for local development unless you harden the configuration separately.
Review Docker Compose commands that remove volumes before approving them.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse the default admin password or database passwords.
Do not run destructive Docker volume commands without a current backup.
Do not treat the local Docker templates as production security configuration.

faq.question: What does this skill install?
faq.answer: It provides templates and commands for a local WordPress stack using Docker Compose, MariaDB, WordPress, and WP-CLI.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this production ready?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for local development and needs hardening before any production use.

faq.question: Does it require Docker?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflows depend on Docker Compose and containerized WordPress services.

faq.question: Does it manage plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes WP-CLI commands to install, activate, list, and update WordPress plugins.

faq.question: What should I check before running it?
faq.answer: Review credentials, exposed ports, volume removal commands, and any plugin list before approving execution.
